newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gilts to head down to 113-22.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gilts to head down to 113-22.

text.p: September gilt futures will continue to move lower on Wednesday prompted by weakness in other bond markets, technical analysts said.

"The Bunds are very weak and T-bonds also look capable of going lower. That kind of background makes it very difficult for gilts although in isolation they do not so bad," said David Wood, an independant technical analyst near London.
"With the position on the Bund and T-bond at the moment there is every chance that we are going to reach 113-30 to 113-22."
At 0709 GMT, September gilts were at 114-07, down 2/32.
On Tuesday, Wood said gilts had come to rest on a trend channel which would come in around 114-07 for this session. But pressure from other markets was likely to force gilts lower.
He said the high 113s had been a good area of support in early July.
"We look pretty soft today below 114-13, 17 area," he said. "But we shouldn't go through that big support in the high 113s, it seems too aggresive."
To the upside, Wood said if the contract managed to break and hold above 114-13 there was a tough band of resistance from 114-27 up to 115-00.
"That ought to cap the upside and it will be a bit of a grind to get up there," he said.
Technical analysts at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London also said the 114-13, 17 region would revert to resistance and prevent initial upticks extending to 114-27, 28.

"It would take a recovery above the latter to leave a more supportive tone, while a rotation above the 115-11 level would be needed to revive potential to retest the contract highs," they said in a research note.
They did not favour a recovery and said losses through 114-00 looked increasingly likely.
"Once this gives way look for more aggressive declines to 113-16, and even 113-01/112-19," they said.
At the short end, December short sterling was at 92.53, up three basis points on the day.
